# Krishiv configuration reference

<!-- @generated by `cargo xtask docs-config`; do not edit. -->

Keys under `krishiv.experimental.` are experimental and off by default. Spark aliases are accepted in place of the Krishiv key; other unknown `spark.*` keys produce a warning, unknown `krishiv.*` keys an error.

| Key | Type | Default | Scope | Settable by | Since | Spark alias | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `krishiv.agent.gateBytes` | size | `1GB` | session | admin | 0.1.0 |  | Agent mode (`krishiv sql --agent`, the REPL's agent output, MCP): a statement whose estimated table scans reach this many bytes is not run; the answer is the estimate and the plan outline, and the caller repeats it with `--allow-heavy` to run it anyway. A statement whose tables report no statistics runs. 0 turns the gate off. |
| `krishiv.cache.maxBytes` | size | `512MB` | session | admin | 0.1.0 |  | Most bytes cached relations (`DataFrame.cache`, `persist`) may hold in memory, per session, as Arrow batches under the `relation_cache` memory pool. Materialization is lazy (on first use) and all-or-nothing: when caching a relation would exceed the cap, the query runs uncached instead of failing. `0` disables caching: queries always run uncached. |
| `krishiv.connect.address` | string | `127.0.0.1` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 | `spark.connect.grpc.binding.address` | The address the Spark Connect listener binds. Loopback by default (Spark binds every interface); a non-loopback address needs authentication configured, or the server refuses to start. |
| `krishiv.connect.handshakeTimeout` | duration | `10s` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | A new Spark Connect connection that sends no first byte for this long is closed, so silent sockets cannot hold `krishiv.connect.maxConnections` for longer. `0s` means no deadline. |
| `krishiv.connect.http2.maxConcurrentStreams` | positive int | `100` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | Most concurrent RPCs (HTTP/2 streams) on one Spark Connect connection; more are refused. |
| `krishiv.connect.http2.maxHeaderListBytes` | size | `16KB` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | The largest header list of a Spark Connect request. |
| `krishiv.connect.http2.maxPendingAcceptResets` | positive int | `20` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | Streams a client may open and reset before the server accepts them, before the connection is closed (the HTTP/2 rapid-reset bound). |
| `krishiv.connect.keepAlive.enabled` | bool | `true` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 | `spark.connect.grpc.keepAlive.enabled` | Whether the server pings idle Spark Connect connections to find dead clients. |
| `krishiv.connect.keepAlive.time` | duration | `1min` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 | `spark.connect.grpc.keepAlive.time` | How often the server pings an idle Spark Connect connection. |
| `krishiv.connect.keepAlive.timeout` | duration | `20s` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 | `spark.connect.grpc.keepAlive.timeout` | How long the server waits for a keepalive answer before it closes the connection. |
| `krishiv.connect.maxConnections` | positive int | `1024` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | Most open Spark Connect connections; past it the server accepts no new one until one closes. |
| `krishiv.connect.maxInboundMessageSize` | size | `128MB` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 | `spark.connect.grpc.maxInboundMessageSize` | The largest Spark Connect request message; a larger one is refused before it is read. |
| `krishiv.connect.maxSessions` | positive int | `1000` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | Most live Spark Connect sessions in the server; a new one past it is refused with `KRISHIV_SESSION_LIMIT`. |
| `krishiv.connect.maxSessionsPerPrincipal` | positive int | `100` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | Most live Spark Connect sessions of one principal; a new one past it is refused with `KRISHIV_SESSION_LIMIT`. |
| `krishiv.connect.port` | positive int | `15002` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 | `spark.connect.grpc.binding.port` | The port `krishiv server` serves Spark Connect on (`sc://host:15002`). A port in use fails the start. |
| `krishiv.connect.session.closedTombstones` | int | `1000` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 | `spark.connect.session.manager.closedSessionsTombstonesSize` | How many released Spark Connect session ids are remembered, so reusing one answers `INVALID_HANDLE.SESSION_CLOSED`; the least recently used is forgotten first. |
| `krishiv.connect.session.idleTimeout` | duration | `1h` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | A Spark Connect session no RPC used for this long is released (its id then answers `INVALID_HANDLE.SESSION_CLOSED`); a session running a query is kept. `0s` never expires (Spark's `spark.connect.session.manager.defaultSessionTimeout`, whose `-1` this is). |
| `krishiv.connect.session.maintenanceInterval` | duration (bare number: ms) | `30s` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 | `spark.connect.session.manager.maintenanceInterval` | How often the server looks for idle Spark Connect sessions to release. |
| `krishiv.deterministicOrder` | bool | `false` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Make a query's result reproducible: every pipeline runs on one driver, so partial states (a decimal `sum` or `avg`, whose overflow can depend on the order of the merges) are merged in the order the input arrives and a query without `ORDER BY` returns its rows in the same order on every run, byte for byte, for the engine's own scans. The key hashes take a fixed seed, so an operator that spills splits its rows the same way on every run. Costs the parallelism of the query: meant for reproducing a result, comparing two builds, and tests. Memory pressure from other queries in the process can still change when an operator spills, and so the order of what it returns. The branches of a `UNION ALL` under an operator that must see all of them (a hash join probing a union) take turns, one after another, so they lose their overlap too. Off by default. |
| `krishiv.exec.agg.directKeys` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.2.0 |  | Internal: a grouped aggregation whose key columns in a batch are all one-byte strings or small integers without NULLs finds each row's group through a table indexed by the packed key, and hashes only each new key's first row. Results are the same either way; false hashes every row. |
| `krishiv.exec.agg.rowLayout` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Internal: grouped aggregations keep their keys as fixed-width rows in radix-partitioned tables and merge the partitions in parallel. Results are the same either way; aggregations with nested or dictionary keys keep the columnar path. |
| `krishiv.exec.batchSize` | int | `4096` | session | admin | 0.1.0 |  | Rows per batch passed between operators. Operators do about a millisecond of work per batch, so the scheduler can switch tasks between batches. |
| `krishiv.exec.debug.planRoundTrip` | bool | `false` | session | admin | 0.1.0 |  | Internal, for tests: every query's physical plan is encoded to the `krishiv.plan.v1` wire format and decoded again before it runs, as a worker would receive it. A plan the format cannot carry, or one that decodes to a different plan, fails the query. Results are the same either way. |
| `krishiv.exec.join.buildProjection` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Internal: an expression above an inner hash join that reads only the build input's columns, cannot raise and is narrower than the columns it frees is computed on the build input, so the hash table holds its result instead of those columns. Results are the same either way; false computes it above the join. |
| `krishiv.exec.join.buildSide` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Internal: a semi, anti or left outer join whose right input is estimated much larger than its left builds its hash table from the left input (a right semi, right anti or right outer join). Results are the same either way; false keeps Spark's side (the right input). |
| `krishiv.exec.join.fuseProbeSelect` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.2.0 |  | Internal: a filter directly below a hash join's probe side, and a scan's runtime filters there, run inside the probe, which then joins the rows they keep without copying them first. Results are the same either way; turn it off to plan the filter as an operator of its own and keep the runtime filters in the scan. |
| `krishiv.exec.join.idleSpillAfter` | duration | `1s` | session | admin | 0.1.0 |  | How long a finished hash join build table may wait for its probe side to start before it counts as idle. When memory runs short, an idle table is spilled first, one partition at a time, before an operator that is running spills its own state; the probe reads the spilled partitions back from disk. A shorter wait keeps less memory idle; a longer one spills less often when the probe starts soon. |
| `krishiv.exec.join.radixBits` | int | `3` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Internal: a row-layout hash join build splits its rows into 2^bits partitions by the top bits of the key hash (3 to 6) and indexes them in parallel. Results are the same for every value. |
| `krishiv.exec.join.rowLayout` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Internal: hash joins store their keys as fixed-width rows and index them with a table that switches by size between a flat and a salted directory. Results are the same either way; joins whose key types have no row encoding keep the columnar path. |
| `krishiv.exec.join.sharedBroadcastBytes` | size | `0B` | session | admin | 0.1.0 |  | Bytes the broadcast join tables one query shares among its tasks on a worker may hold; 0 sets no cap beyond the query's memory. A shared build that grows past it stops, and each task of the query builds its own table from the broadcast rows instead, spilling as needed. A cap below the query's memory avoids the spill of the query's other memory that precedes that fallback when the table does not fit. |
| `krishiv.exec.join.smj.bufferBytes` | size | `0B` | session | admin | 0.1.0 |  | Bytes of one join key's right-side rows a sort-merge join keeps in memory before it moves them to a spill file; 0 takes a share of the memory pool. Spark bounds these rows by count (`spark.sql.sortMergeJoinExec.buffer.in.memory.threshold` and `spark.sql.sortMergeJoinExec.buffer.spill.threshold`), which have no effect here. |
| `krishiv.exec.join.strategy` | enum (`auto`, `sortMerge`) | `auto` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Internal: `auto` runs equi-joins as hash joins unless a `MERGE` hint asks otherwise; `sortMerge` runs every equi-join without a strategy hint as a sort-merge join, except `NOT IN` and keys that cannot be ordered. Results are the same either way. |
| `krishiv.exec.lateFetch.maxRows` | int | `50` | session | admin | 0.1.0 |  | Most rows (limit plus offset) an ORDER BY ... LIMIT over a file scan may rank while reading only the sort keys and filter columns, fetching the other columns for the rows kept; 0 turns it off. Results are the same either way. |
| `krishiv.exec.seed` | int | (none) | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Internal, for tests: seeds the key hashes of grouped aggregations and joins and the order in which scan morsels are claimed, and runs aggregations in their deterministic mode, so that the order of groups and of unordered `LIMIT` rows is the same on every run. Unset, each query draws a random seed. |
| `krishiv.exec.sort.hashBuckets` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Internal: the sort below a window with a PARTITION BY splits its rows into buckets by the hash of the partitioning keys and sorts, merges and evaluates the buckets in parallel. Results are the same either way. |
| `krishiv.exec.targetPartitionBytes` | size | `128MB` | session | admin | 0.1.0 |  | Target size of a partition for scans and exchanges. |
| `krishiv.experimental.ivm` | bool | `false` | session | admin | 0.1.0 |  | Experimental: incremental maintenance of materialized views. |
| `krishiv.experimental.unalignedCheckpoints` | bool | `false` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Experimental: allow unaligned checkpoints under sustained backpressure. |
| `krishiv.io.blockingThreads` | positive int | `8` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Most blocking threads of the I/O runtime, where local-file reads and writes run: at most this many local-file requests run at once per executor (`krishiv.io.maxConcurrentRequests` still bounds those in flight). Each such thread keeps freed read buffers in its own allocator cache, so the bound also bounds that memory. Read when the session starts its executor. |
| `krishiv.io.cache.blockBytes` | size | `1MB` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Size of the aligned blocks the cache stores and fetches; a read is served from the blocks it overlaps. |
| `krishiv.io.cache.diskBytes` | size | `10GB` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Size cap of the block cache's disk part; the least recently used blocks are removed to stay under it (it may exceed the cap by one block while a block is written). |
| `krishiv.io.cache.enabled` | bool | `false` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Cache the byte ranges read from remote object stores (data pages, footers and page indexes alike) in aligned blocks on local disk, with a small in-memory tier in front. A block is keyed by the store, the path, the object's version (ETag or modification time) and the block index, so an overwritten object never serves old bytes. The disk part starts empty and is removed when the session ends. Any cache failure falls back to the store. Local files are never cached. |
| `krishiv.io.cache.memoryBytes` | size | `64MB` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Size of the block cache's in-memory tier (least recently used blocks). `0` keeps blocks on disk only. |
| `krishiv.io.cache.path` | string | (none) | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Directory of the block cache's disk part (a local SSD). Each cache uses a subdirectory of its own, empties it when created and removes it when dropped; subdirectories no running cache holds any longer are removed too. When unset: `krishiv-block-cache-<uid>` under the system temp directory (a directory this user does not own is refused). |
| `krishiv.io.coalesceBytes` | size | `1MB` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Byte ranges of one file closer than this are fetched with one request, as long as the request reads few enough bytes outside the ranges (`krishiv.io.coalesceWasteBytes`, `krishiv.io.coalesceWasteDivisor`). |
| `krishiv.io.coalesceWasteBytes` | size | (none) | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Bytes outside the requested ranges that any coalesced read may fetch (besides `krishiv.io.coalesceWasteDivisor`'s share). A read's whole span is reserved while it is in flight, so this trades bytes read for fewer requests. When unset: 64 KiB for local files, 1 MiB for object stores and HTTP, where a request costs latency. |
| `krishiv.io.coalesceWasteDivisor` | positive int | `16` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | A coalesced read may fetch up to 1/this of its bytes outside the requested ranges (or `krishiv.io.coalesceWasteBytes`, whichever is larger). |
| `krishiv.io.credentials.refreshSkew` | duration | `5min` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | How long before its expiry a short-lived object-store credential (vended by a catalog or a token service) is refreshed. A request that arrives inside this window fetches a new credential first; an expired credential is never used. `0s` refreshes only at expiry. |
| `krishiv.io.footerReadBytes` | size | `64KB` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Size of the speculative read at the end of a file that fetches its footer in one request; a format may ask for more (up to 1 MiB). |
| `krishiv.io.lateMaterialization` | enum (`auto`, `on`, `off`) | `auto` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Whether a Parquet scan evaluates its pushed filter on the filter's columns before decoding the others for the rows that pass: `auto` decides per row group from the fraction of rows the filter kept before, `on` and `off` force it. Returned rows are the same either way; with the filter, decode errors confined to rows it rejects (a corrupt page or invalid UTF-8 in a column it does not read) are not raised. |
| `krishiv.io.maxConcurrentRequests` | int | `64` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Most object-store requests in flight at once per store, over all queries of the process. The local file store also runs each request on a blocking thread of the I/O runtime, so at most `krishiv.io.blockingThreads` of them run at once. |
| `krishiv.io.maxRequestBytes` | size | `16MB` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Ranges are not coalesced into requests larger than this (a single larger range is still fetched whole). |
| `krishiv.io.maxRetries` | int | `5` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Retries of an object-store request that failed transiently (throttling, unavailable, timeout), with jittered exponential backoff honouring `Retry-After`. |
| `krishiv.io.metadataCacheBytes` | size | `64MB` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Size of the in-memory cache of decoded file footers and metadata (least recently used entries are evicted). `0` disables it. |
| `krishiv.io.multipartPartBytes` | size | `8MB` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Part size of multipart uploads (at least 5 MiB; doubled every 1,000 parts so a file never needs more than the 10,000 parts object stores allow). |
| `krishiv.io.parquet.bloomFilter.enabled` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Whether a Parquet scan reads the stored Bloom filters of the row groups its statistics could not decide and skips a row group when a pushed equality or IN literal cannot be in it. Returned rows are the same either way: the filter only prunes, and a filter that fails a check is ignored. Files without Bloom filters pay nothing. |
| `krishiv.io.parquet.dictionaryFilter.enabled` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.2.0 |  | Whether a Parquet scan reads the dictionary page of a column chunk whose data pages are all dictionary encoded, for the row groups its statistics could not decide, and skips a row group when the dictionary holds no literal of a pushed equality or IN. Returned rows are the same either way: the dictionary only prunes, and a page that fails a check is ignored. Dictionary pages above 16 MiB are not read. |
| `krishiv.io.parquet.pageIndex.enabled` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Whether a Parquet scan reads the page index of the row groups its statistics could not decide and skips the pages the pushed filter rules out. Returned rows are the same either way: the index only prunes, and an index that fails a check is ignored. Files without a page index pay nothing. |
| `krishiv.io.prefetchBytes` | size | `64MB` | session | admin | 0.1.0 |  | Bytes a file scan may fetch ahead of decoding, per scan driver. Prefetched bytes are reserved from the query's memory pool and dropped first under memory pressure. |
| `krishiv.io.requestTimeout` | duration | `30s` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Timeout of one object-store request attempt; a timed-out attempt is retried. |
| `krishiv.io.strictOptions` | bool | `false` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | When true, a data source option that the format does not know is an error (`KRISHIV_UNKNOWN_FORMAT_OPTION`). When false (the default, as in Spark), it is ignored with a warning that suggests the closest known option. |
| `krishiv.memory.abortReleaseTimeout` | duration | `30s` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | How long a memory request waits for queries the arbitrator aborted to release their memory; aborted queries release at their next batch boundary. While their memory covers the request, no other query is aborted. The request fails after this time. |
| `krishiv.memory.limit` | size | (none) | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Memory available to query execution in this process: the limit of the root memory pool. Operators reserve memory before allocating and spill when the limit is reached. When unset: 80% of the effective memory limit (the tightest cgroup limit, else physical memory), or 2 GiB where that cannot be determined. |
| `krishiv.memory.reservationQuantum` | size | `1MB` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Granularity of memory reservations: a consumer takes memory from its pools in steps of this size (at most 1/64 of the smallest pool limit above it), so small reservations rarely touch shared counters. Unused parts of a step are reclaimed before anything is spilled. `1b` disables rounding. |
| `krishiv.memory.residentGuard` | bool | `true` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Whether the root memory pool keeps what the process holds beyond its reservations (allocator overhead, memory used without a reservation) within an allowance of 1/8 of the limit plus 64 MiB, by lowering the memory ordinary reservations may take so operators spill. It needs a resident-set probe from the program that owns the allocator: the `krishiv` CLI and the bench runner install one when started with a limit below 4 GiB; elsewhere the setting has no effect. Spill I/O and arbitration rounds whose spills are exhausted are exempt from it. |
| `krishiv.memory.spillScratchReserve` | size | `512KB` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Memory at the top of every limited memory pool (at most 1/8 of its limit) that only spill writers' scratch buffers may use, so a full pool can still fund the spill that frees it. Shared by every spill under the pool and released when each write ends. `0` disables it. |
| `krishiv.memory.spillWaitTimeout` | duration | `2s` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | How long the memory arbitrator waits for a consumer asked to spill to begin spilling before it gives up on it and aborts the query furthest above its fair share of memory. A spill that has begun is awaited to its end. |
| `krishiv.metrics.enabled` | bool | `false` | session | admin | 0.1.0 |  | When true, every query that reaches execution folds its metrics into the engine's metrics registry once, at query end (`Session::metrics`, `krishiv.metrics()`); when false the fold is skipped entirely. Engine gauges (memory, spill disk, metadata cache size, build info) are evaluated when the snapshot is read either way. |
| `krishiv.network.timeout` | duration | `2min` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 | `spark.network.timeout` | Default timeout for network interactions between cluster processes. |
| `krishiv.optimizer.eagerAggregation` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Run an aggregate's calls below a join and merge their states above it, when statistics show the join keeps most rows and the join keys group them well. Only calls whose result cannot depend on row order or raise on a row the join would drop are moved. Results are the same either way. |
| `krishiv.optimizer.joinCost` | enum (`rows`, `bytes`) | `rows` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | What the join optimizer minimises when it orders a tree of inner joins, and which input of each join it builds. `rows`: the rows of the intermediate results; the input with fewer rows is built; when two orders cost the same rows (to a relative 1e-9), the one whose builds hold fewer bytes wins. `bytes`: each join's result rows times 48 bytes plus the bytes of its build input (rows times the estimated width of the columns still read, Spark's default size per type); the input with fewer rows is built unless it holds more than twice the other's bytes. Results are the same either way. |
| `krishiv.optimizer.joinDpLimit` | positive int | `10` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Most inputs of an inner-join tree the `dpsub` join enumerator plans exactly; larger trees are planned greedily. Values above 14 count as 14: the work grows as 3 to the power of the inputs. Results are the same either way. |
| `krishiv.optimizer.joinEnumerator` | enum (`dpsub`, `greedy`) | `dpsub` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | How the join optimizer orders each tree of inner joins. `dpsub`: dynamic programming over every split of every subset of the inputs, for trees of at most `krishiv.optimizer.joinDpLimit` inputs, greedy above. `greedy`: always join the connected pair with the fewest result rows. Results are the same either way; for comparing plans and planning time. |
| `krishiv.optimizer.ndvSampling.enabled` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Before a query is optimized, count the distinct values of the file columns an equality or IN compares with values, when the files store no distinct count, from the first rows of the table's files. The count steers join ordering and build-side choice; results are the same either way. Samples are kept per file version. |
| `krishiv.optimizer.ndvSampling.rows` | positive int | `131072` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | The most rows a distinct-value sample of a table reads, from its first files in order. A table no larger than this is counted exactly. |
| `krishiv.optimizer.ndvSampling.timeout` | duration | `5s` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | The time one query's distinct-value samples may take together: its tables are sampled in turn, each with what the ones before it left. A table that runs out of time, or gets none, keeps its default estimates; EXPLAIN COST and EXPLAIN VERBOSE say which ("Distinct-Value Samples"). The row limit is what bounds a sample; this only guards against slow storage, so that how fast the machine is does not decide the plan. |
| `krishiv.optimizer.shareRepeatedSubtrees` | bool | `false` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Compute an uncorrelated subtree once when the main block reads it directly and a subquery reads it again (TPC-H q11), and let both read the stored result. Needs `krishiv.sql.optimizer.shareCteInstances`. Results are the same either way. Off by default. |
| `krishiv.optimizer.subqueryAsWindow` | bool | `false` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Compute a correlated scalar aggregate subquery over the same relations and filters as the outer block (TPC-H q17, q02) as a window over the outer join's rows, so the big table is read once. Only `min`, `max` and exact decimal `avg` of non-floating, non-collated keys qualify, and only when statistics say the rewrite pays. Results are the same either way. Off by default. |
| `krishiv.python.udf.threads` | int | `0` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Threads of the embedded Python UDF pool, fixed when the pool starts (the first query calling a Python UDF). 0 picks one: the executor's thread count on a free-threaded Python, else 1 (with the GIL more threads only contend). |
| `krishiv.query.maxExecutionTime` | duration | (none) | session | user | 0.2.0 |  | The longest a query may run from the start of its execution: past it the query is cancelled and fails with `KRISHIV_QUERY_TIMEOUT`. The limit is read when the query starts. For a SQL script, the whole script is the query: the limit counts from its start. When unset, queries run without a time limit. |
| `krishiv.query.maxQueuedTime` | duration | (none) | session | user | 0.2.0 |  | Reserved: the longest a query may wait for admission before it starts. No admission queue exists yet, so the value is accepted and has no effect. |
| `krishiv.resultCache.enabled` | bool | `false` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Keep the rows of a query for later runs of the same query by any session of the process with the same principal and access-policy version. Only queries over permanent catalog tables with no non-deterministic function are cached. Entries are dropped by `REFRESH TABLE`, `CLEAR CACHE` and every write the engine commits to a table they read; a change made outside the engine is not seen until the entry expires. Off by default. |
| `krishiv.resultCache.maxBytes` | size | `64MB` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Most bytes the result cache of an engine runtime holds (the process-wide store of sessions built alone, or a supplied runtime's own), as Arrow batches outside the query memory pool; fixed when the runtime is built. A result larger than the cap is not stored; when a new result would pass the cap the oldest entries go first, and entries past their ttl go whenever a result is stored. Needs `krishiv.resultCache.enabled`. |
| `krishiv.resultCache.ttl` | duration | `1d` | session | admin | 0.1.0 |  | How long the result cache serves an entry, counted from when it was stored; an older entry is dropped before the next lookup and the query runs again. `0s` never expires. Needs `krishiv.resultCache.enabled`. |
| `krishiv.runtimeFilter.adaptive.maxPassPercent` | int | `90` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | A scan driver stops evaluating a runtime filter on rows once it passes more than this percentage of a measurement window (pruning splits and row groups with it continues). |
| `krishiv.runtimeFilter.adaptive.minRows` | int | `65536` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Rows per window over which a scan driver measures a runtime filter's pass rate. |
| `krishiv.runtimeFilter.bloom.maxBytes` | size | `8MB` | session | admin | 0.1.0 |  | Largest runtime Bloom filter. A filter capped below its 1% false-positive size is still built unless its expected false-positive rate exceeds 5%. |
| `krishiv.runtimeFilter.bloom.maxItems` | int | `4000000` | session | admin | 0.1.0 |  | Most build keys a runtime Bloom filter is built for: a build estimated larger plans none, and one that turns out larger publishes none. |
| `krishiv.runtimeFilter.bloom.minApplicationRows` | int | `1000000` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | A runtime Bloom filter is planned only for a scan estimated at this many rows or more (and at least four times the build). |
| `krishiv.runtimeFilter.enabled` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Plan runtime filters: the build side of an inner or left semi hash join publishes the min/max, a small value set or a Bloom filter of its keys to the scans feeding the probe side, which skip splits, row groups and rows no build key can match. Results are the same either way. |
| `krishiv.runtimeFilter.exactSet.maxValues` | int | `4096` | session | admin | 0.1.0 |  | Most distinct build keys a runtime filter tests rows against exactly (a small set or a hash set); with more, a Bloom filter (when planned) or only the min/max range is used on rows. |
| `krishiv.runtimeFilter.inList.maxValues` | int | `50` | session | admin | 0.1.0 |  | Most distinct build keys a runtime filter keeps as a value set; with more, a Bloom filter (when planned) or only the min/max range is published. |
| `krishiv.server.allowCoreDumps` | bool | `false` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | Whether `krishiv server` may write a core dump. Off by default: a dump holds query data and credentials. |
| `krishiv.server.metrics.public` | bool | `false` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | Whether the admin server's `/metrics` answers without the admin token. Only on a loopback address; aggregate counters only. |
| `krishiv.server.shutdownTimeout` | duration | `30s` | cluster | startup | 0.3.0 |  | On SIGTERM or SIGINT, how long running queries may finish before every session is closed and its queries cancelled. New requests are refused at once. |
| `krishiv.session.memoryLimit` | size | (none) | session | admin | 0.2.0 |  | Memory the queries of one session may hold together: the limit of the session's own pool under the process root (`krishiv.memory.limit` still bounds the process). A request over it spills, then cancels one of the session's own queries, never another session's. Fixed when the session is built. When unset, a session's queries are bounded by the process limit only. |
| `krishiv.spill.compression` | enum (`lz4`, `zstd`, `none`) | `lz4` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Compression of the Arrow IPC buffers in spill files: `lz4` (fastest), `zstd` (smaller files, more CPU) or `none`. Files are self-describing, so the setting only affects files written afterwards. |
| `krishiv.spill.dir` | string | (none) | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Directory for spill files (operator state written to local disk under memory pressure). Each process creates its own subdirectory and removes it on exit; subdirectories left behind by crashed processes are removed at the next start. When unset: the first of `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` (or `~/.cache`) `/krishiv/spill`, `/var/tmp/krishiv-spill-<uid>` and `<temp dir>/krishiv-spill-<uid>` that is not on a RAM file system (tmpfs). Prefer a local SSD; network and FUSE file systems are refused. |
| `krishiv.spill.dropBehindBytes` | size | `8MB` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | How many bytes a spill writer writes before it asks the kernel to write them to disk and drop them from the page cache (Linux). Dirty spill pages count against a memory cgroup's limit and cannot be reclaimed until written back, so without this a spilling query can push its cgroup into the OOM killer. A finished file is written back and dropped too. `0` disables it; other platforms ignore it. |
| `krishiv.spill.maxBytes` | size | `64GB` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Most bytes spill files may occupy on disk at once, over all queries of the process. A spill that would exceed it fails with `KRISHIV_SPILL_CAP_EXCEEDED`. |
| `krishiv.spill.zstd.level` | int | `1` | cluster | startup | 0.1.0 |  | Zstandard compression level for spill files when `krishiv.spill.compression` is `zstd`: 1 is fastest; higher levels (up to 22) give smaller files and cost more CPU. Levels from -131072 (ultra-fast) are accepted. |
| `krishiv.sql.ansi.enabled` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.1.0 | `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` | When true, follow ANSI SQL semantics: invalid casts and arithmetic overflow raise errors instead of returning NULL. |
| `krishiv.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold` | signed size | `10485760` | session | admin | 0.1.0 | `spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold` | The largest estimated size, in bytes, of a join input that is broadcast to every task without a hint. A negative value turns broadcasting by size off; a `BROADCAST` hint still broadcasts. |
| `krishiv.sql.avro.compression.codec` | enum (`uncompressed`, `deflate`, `snappy`, `bzip2`, `xz`, `zstandard`) | `snappy` | session | user | 0.1.0 | `spark.sql.avro.compression.codec` | The block codec of Avro files written without a `compression` option. | `krishiv.sql.avro.datetimeRebaseModeInRead` | enum (`EXCEPTION`, `CORRECTED`, `LEGACY`) | `EXCEPTION` | session | user | 0.1.0 | `spark.sql.avro.datetimeRebaseModeInRead` | How an Avro read treats dates and timestamps before 1582-10-15 in files whose writer is unknown (files written by Spark 3.0 or later say how they were written): `EXCEPTION` fails, `CORRECTED` reads the stored values, `LEGACY` is refused. | `krishiv.sql.binaryOutputStyle` | enum (`UTF-8`, `BASIC`, `BASE64`, `HEX`, `HEX_DISCRETE`) | (none) | session | user | 0.2.0 | `spark.sql.binaryOutputStyle` | How `to_csv` and `to_xml` print a `BINARY` value: `UTF-8` text, `BASIC` signed byte values (`[69, 97]`), `BASE64` without padding, `HEX` (`4561`) or `HEX_DISCRETE` (`[45 61]`). | `krishiv.sql.collation.schemaLevel.enabled` | bool | `false` | session | user | 0.2.0 | `spark.sql.collation.schemaLevel.enabled` | Whether a schema may have a default collation (`CREATE SCHEMA .. DEFAULT COLLATION`, `ALTER SCHEMA .. DEFAULT COLLATION`). Off, as in Spark 4.2, the clause is `UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE.SCHEMA_LEVEL_COLLATIONS`. On, the schema stores it and `DESCRIBE SCHEMA` shows it; tables, views and functions are not created in such a schema yet (Spark gives their strings the schema's collation; Krishiv does not apply it). |
| `krishiv.sql.cteRecursionLevelLimit` | int | `100` | session | admin | 0.1.0 | `spark.sql.cteRecursionLevelLimit` | Most rounds a recursive common table expression may run before the query fails with RECURSION_LEVEL_LIMIT_EXCEEDED; -1 removes the limit. A MAX RECURSION LEVEL clause on the expression overrides it. |
| `krishiv.sql.cteRecursionRowLimit` | int | `1000000` | session | admin | 0.1.0 | `spark.sql.cteRecursionRowLimit` | Most rows a recursive common table expression may produce in all rounds before the query fails with RECURSION_ROW_LIMIT_EXCEEDED; -1 removes the limit. |
| `krishiv.sql.defaultPath` | string | `` | session | user | 0.1.0 | `spark.sql.defaultPath` | What `DEFAULT_PATH` expands to: a comma-separated `SET PATH` element list without `PATH`. Empty means `system.builtin, system.session, current_schema`. |
| `krishiv.sql.execution.arrow.maxRecordsPerBatch` | int | `10000` | session | user | 0.1.0 | `spark.sql.execution.arrow.maxRecordsPerBatch` | Most rows in one Arrow batch handed to a Python UDF; zero or a negative value means no limit (the input batches are passed as they are). |
| `krishiv.sql.execution.pythonUDF.arrow.enabled` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.1.0 | `spark.sql.execution.pythonUDF.arrow.enabled` | Whether `@udf` Python UDFs run Arrow-batched. Only the Arrow path is implemented: `false` is accepted with a warning and still runs Arrow-batched, whose return-type coercion differs from Spark's pickled-row path in some cases (a documented divergence). |
| `krishiv.sql.files.commitProtocol` | enum (`AUTO`, `LOG`, `NONE`) | `AUTO` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | How a write to a plain directory is committed: `LOG` records every commit in `_krishiv_log/` (put-if-absent, so concurrent writers cannot both take a version), and Krishiv readers of the directory then see only committed files; `NONE` is Spark's plain commit (files under their final names, `_SUCCESS`); `AUTO` (the default) uses the log where the store supports put-if-absent and the plain commit, with a warning, where it does not. A directory that already has a `_krishiv_log/` keeps being written through it, whatever this is set to (`NONE` does not switch an existing log off). |
| `krishiv.sql.files.maxPartitionBytes` | size | `128MB` | session | admin | 0.1.0 | `spark.sql.files.maxPartitionBytes` | Most bytes packed into one file-scan partition (Spark's split planning). |
| `krishiv.sql.files.maxPartitionNum` | positive int | (none) | session | admin | 0.1.0 | `spark.sql.files.maxPartitionNum` | Suggested maximum number of file-scan partitions: when splitting yields more, the split size is raised so that about this many remain. Unset: no maximum. |
| `krishiv.sql.files.minPartitionNum` | positive int | (none) | session | admin | 0.1.0 | `spark.sql.files.minPartitionNum` | Suggested minimum number of file-scan partitions. When unset: `krishiv.sql.leafNodeDefaultParallelism`, else the number of worker slots. |
| `krishiv.sql.files.openCostInBytes` | size | `4MB` | session | user | 0.1.0 | `spark.sql.files.openCostInBytes` | Estimated cost of opening a file, in bytes that could be scanned in the same time; added per file when files are packed into scan partitions. |
| `krishiv.sql.leafNodeDefaultParallelism` | positive int | (none) | session | admin | 0.1.0 | `spark.sql.leafNodeDefaultParallelism` | Default parallelism of leaf scans (used when `krishiv.sql.files.minPartitionNum` is unset). When unset: the number of worker slots. |
| `krishiv.sql.legacy.codingErrorAction` | bool | `false` | session | user | 0.1.0 | `spark.sql.legacy.codingErrorAction` | When true, `encode` writes `?` for a character the charset cannot hold and `decode` reads malformed input as U+FFFD; when false both raise `MALFORMED_CHARACTER_CODING`. |
| `krishiv.sql.legacy.ctePrecedencePolicy` | enum (`EXCEPTION`, `LEGACY`, `CORRECTED`) | `CORRECTED` | session | user | 0.1.0 | `spark.sql.legacy.ctePrecedencePolicy` | How nested WITH definitions with the same name resolve: EXCEPTION fails on a nested definition shadowing an outer one, LEGACY inlines outer definitions first, CORRECTED lets inner definitions shadow outer ones. |
| `krishiv.sql.legacy.javaCharsets` | bool | `false` | session | user | 0.1.0 | `spark.sql.legacy.javaCharsets` | When true, `encode` and `decode` also accept `windows-1252` and the ISO-8859 family under Java's names; other Java charsets are not supported. | `krishiv.sql.legacy.skipTypeValidationOnAlterPartition` | bool | `false` | session | user | 0.2.0 | `spark.sql.legacy.skipTypeValidationOnAlterPartition` | When true, the partition values of `ALTER TABLE .. ADD PARTITION`, `DROP PARTITION` and `RENAME PARTITION` are kept as written instead of being cast to the partition column types (`'007'` stays `007`, `'abc'` for an INT column is accepted). |
| `krishiv.sql.legacy.statisticalAggregate` | bool | `false` | session | user | 0.1.0 | `spark.sql.legacy.statisticalAggregate` | When true, `stddev_samp`, `var_samp`, `covar_samp` and `corr` of a single row, and `skewness` and `kurtosis` of values without variance, return NaN; when false they return NULL, as Spark 4 does. |
| `krishiv.sql.legacy.timeParserPolicy` | enum (`EXCEPTION`, `CORRECTED`, `LEGACY`) | `EXCEPTION` | session | user | 0.1.0 | `spark.sql.legacy.timeParserPolicy` | How the datetime pattern functions (`date_format`, `to_date`, `to_timestamp`, `unix_timestamp`, `from_unixtime`) and the JSON, CSV and XML functions read and print patterns. `LEGACY` is the pre-3.0 behaviour: `SimpleDateFormat` for the datetime functions, and a lenient commons-lang `FastDateFormat` for the `DATE` and `TIMESTAMP` fields of the JSON, CSV and XML functions; `CORRECTED` and `EXCEPTION` use the `DateTimeFormatter` patterns. |
| `krishiv.sql.legacy.viewSchemaBindingMode` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.1.0 | `spark.sql.legacy.viewSchemaBindingMode` | When true, a permanent view may take `WITH SCHEMA BINDING \| COMPENSATION \| TYPE EVOLUTION \| EVOLUTION`, records its schema binding mode (shown by `DESCRIBE EXTENDED` and `SHOW CREATE TABLE`) and reads by it; a view stored without a mode reads as `BINDING`. When false, the clause is `FEATURE_NOT_ENABLED` and every view reads as before the modes existed (see `viewSchemaCompensation`). |
| `krishiv.sql.legacy.viewSchemaCompensation` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.1.0 | `spark.sql.legacy.viewSchemaCompensation` | When true, a view created without `WITH SCHEMA` is `COMPENSATION` (a changed column type is cast to the stored one with an ANSI cast) and a view without a mode casts so when `viewSchemaBindingMode` is false; when false, such views are `BINDING` (only up-casts are allowed). |
| `krishiv.sql.mapKeyDedupPolicy` | enum (`EXCEPTION`, `LAST_WIN`) | `EXCEPTION` | session | user | 0.1.0 | `spark.sql.mapKeyDedupPolicy` | How duplicate map keys are handled by the map functions (`map`, `map_concat`, `map_from_arrays`, `map_from_entries`, `str_to_map`): `EXCEPTION` fails the query, `LAST_WIN` keeps the value inserted last. |
| `krishiv.sql.optimizer.runtime.bloomFilter.enabled` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.1.0 | `spark.sql.optimizer.runtime.bloomFilter.enabled` | Allow Bloom filters among the runtime filters a join build publishes (min/max and value sets are not affected). Krishiv's cost model decides when one is built; Spark's creation and application size thresholds are not used. |
| `krishiv.sql.optimizer.shareCteInstances` | bool | `true` | session | user | 0.1.0 |  | Compute a deterministic CTE body once per query when two or more references to it are identical after optimization and the body holds a pipeline breaker (an aggregate, join, window, sort, distinct or set operation); every reference reads the one result. | `krishiv.sql.session.timeZone` | time zone | (none) | session | user | 0.1.0 | `spark.sql.session.timeZone` | Session time zone: a region ID such as `America/Los_Angeles` or a zone offset. When unset, the local system time zone is used, as in Spark. |
| `krishiv.sql.shuffle.partitionsHint` | int | (none) | session | user | 0.1.0 | `spark.sql.shuffle.partitions` | Shuffle partition count requested by the user. Treated as a hint: partitioning is driven by `krishiv.exec.targetPartitionBytes`. |
| `krishiv.sql.sources.bucketing.maxBuckets` | positive int | `100000` | session | admin | 0.1.0 | `spark.sql.sources.bucketing.maxBuckets` | Maximum `CLUSTERED BY ... INTO n BUCKETS` bucket count: a count above it fails with `INVALID_BUCKET_COUNT`. |
